content.comment_body: Hi, I'm having an issue with [product_name] communication. When I connect the Ethernet cable, both the PC's Ethernet card and the input port on the [product_name] repeatedly connect and disconnect at the same time. The PC's Ethernet card activates, identifies the device, then drops the connection. This cycle continues as long as the cable is connected. Could the voltage value affect communication? Could there be a problem with the cable? Or with the LAN? Thanks for any assistance! ...sent from App

Have you checked for an IP conflict? Try changing the IP address of the [product_name] as a test. If you're not using a direct connection and instead have a router, make sure the [product_name]'s IP address is outside of the router's DHCP range. The simplest way to test is to connect the [product_name] to a different PC, if possible, or to swap out the patch cable and retest. Regards, [user_name]

Depending on the type of power supply in your PC, it may produce electrical noise. In this situation, you could use a router to isolate the devices, or connect the grounding terminal near the Ethernet port on the [product_name]. Also, remember the maximum cable length is 100 meters, and this only works with high-quality cabling. If you have electrical noise and poor-quality cable, even 10 meters can cause issues.

analysis.insight_summary: The user reports unstable Ethernet connectivity between their PC and a [product_name] module, with the connection frequently dropping and reconnecting. Discussion points to possible network configuration issues, cable quality, electrical interference, and power supply noise as reasons for the instability. These factors make troubleshooting and maintaining reliable communication difficult.
analysis.user_expectations: The user is looking for a stable Ethernet connection between their PC and the [product_name] module, hoping for a straightforward configuration without repeated disconnections or hardware-related interruptions.
